title.value: BIRB: A Generalization Benchmark for Information Retrieval in Bioacoustics

TLDR.value: A holistic, robust retrieval benchmark for evaluating models' ability to generalize within the context of a collection of rich bioacoustics tasks.

abstract.value: The ability for a machine learning model to cope with differences in training and deployment conditions—e.g. in the presence of distribution shift or the generalization to new classes altogether—is crucial for real-world use cases. However, most empirical work in this area has focused on the image domain with artificial benchmarks constructed to measure individual aspects of generalization. We present BIRB, a complex benchmark centered on the retrieval of bird vocalizations from passively-recorded datasets given focal recordings from a large citizen science corpus available for training. We propose a baseline system for this collection of tasks using representation learning and a nearest-centroid search. Our thorough empirical evaluation and analysis surfaces open research directions, suggesting that BIRB fills the need for a more realistic and complex benchmark to drive progress on robustness to distribution shifts and generalization of ML models.
